questions.q: For routine urine analysis, the recommended sample is:
opts: First morning urine sample collected by midstream technique
Random afternoon sample collected by midstream technique
First morning urine sample drawn from the urobag
Evening sample collected after vigorous exercise
questions.exp: Sample: 1st urine sample of morning → midstream technique. (Book p740)

questions.q: Fill up: Urine must be analysed within ______ hours at room temperature, while the pH should be checked immediately.
questions.exp: Analysis: within 2-4 hours at room temperature (pH to be checked immediately). (Book p740)

questions.q: Up to how long may a urine sample be stored at 2-8°C before analysis?
questions.exp: Storage: 2-8°C upto 12 hours. (Book p740)

questions.q: The preservatives listed for a urine sample are:
questions.exp: Preservation: Formaldehyde, Glutaraldehyde. (Book p740)

questions.q: A marathon runner is scheduled for a routine urine check. To avoid false results from rhabdomyolysis, strenuous physical activity must be avoided for how long before collection?
questions.exp: Strenuous physical activity 72 hrs prior to collection → false results due to rhabdomyolysis. (Book p740)

questions.q: Which statement about urine collection is TRUE?
opts: Collection during menstruation should be avoided
Urine may be collected from the urobag in catheterised patients
Strenuous exercise just before collection improves sample quality
pH can reliably be checked after a day at room temperature
questions.exp: To avoid: strenuous activity 72 hrs prior and collection during menstruation; pH is checked immediately. (Book p740)

questions.q: Fill up: In catheterised patients, urine must always be collected ______ and never from the urobag.
questions.exp: Catheterised patients: always collect fresh urine; do not collect from urobag. (Book p740)

questions.q: Match each urine colour with its listed cause — 1) Green 2) Brown 3) Orange … A) Nitrofurantoin B) Rifampicin, entacapone C) Triamterene (ENaC blocker)
questions.exp: Green – triamterene (ENaC blocker); brown – nitrofurantoin; orange – rifampicin, entacapone (COMT inhibitor). (Book p740)

questions.q: Pink urine on the appearance table is attributed to:
questions.exp: Pink: Desferrioxamine, beetroot. (Book p740)

questions.q: Urine that darkens on long standing points to which drug combination?
questions.exp: Darkening on long standing: Imipenem + cilastatin. (Book p740)

questions.q: Which colour-drug pair is NOT as written in the appearance table?
questions.exp: Desferrioxamine gives pink urine; green is triamterene (ENaC blocker). (Book p740)

questions.q: A pungent urine odour, unless proven otherwise, signifies infection because bacteria generate:
questions.exp: Pungent: infection (unless proven otherwise) d/t ammonia produced by bacteria. (Book p740)

questions.q: Match each odour with its condition — 1) Musty/mousy 2) Curry/maple syrup 3) Sweaty feet … A) Maple syrup urine disease (MSUD) B) Isovaleric acidemia, glutaric aciduria type II C) Phenylketonuria
questions.exp: Musty/mousy – phenylketonuria; curry/maple syrup – MSUD; sweaty feet – isovaleric acidemia, glutaric aciduria type II. (Book p740)

questions.q: A neonate's urine smells of sweaty feet. The differential given is:
opts: Isovaleric acidemia or glutaric aciduria type II
Tyrosinemia type 1 or multiple carboxylase deficiency
questions.exp: Sweaty feet odour: isovaleric acidemia; glutaric aciduria type II. (Book p740)

questions.q: Match each odour with its condition — 1) Cabbage-like / rancid butter 2) Cat urine 3) Swimming pool … A) Hawkinsinuria B) Tyrosinemia type 1 C) Multiple carboxylase deficiency (MCD)
questions.exp: Cabbage-like/rancid butter – tyrosinemia type 1; cat urine – MCD; swimming pool – hawkinsinuria. (Book p741)

questions.q: Match each odour with its condition — 1) Fish urine 2) Sulfurous 3) Sweet … A) Beta ketothiolase deficiency B) Trimethylaminuria C) Cystinuria
questions.exp: Fish urine – trimethylaminuria; sulfurous – cystinuria; sweet – beta ketothiolase deficiency. (Book p741)

questions.q: All of the following odour-disease pairs are as printed EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Acid smell belongs to methyl malonic acidemia; cystinuria gives a sulfurous odour. (Book p741)

questions.q: Which odour statement is TRUE as per the table?
opts: Cat urine odour marks multiple carboxylase deficiency
Swimming pool odour marks tyrosinemia type 1
questions.exp: Cat urine – MCD; cabbage-like/rancid butter – tyrosinemia type 1; swimming pool – hawkinsinuria. (Book p741)

questions.q: Match each parameter with its normal urine value — 1) pH 2) Specific gravity 3) Osmolality (mOsm/kg) … A) 1.020-1.040 B) 800-900 C) 4-4.5 (acidic)
questions.exp: Urine pH 4-4.5 (acidic); specific gravity 1.020-1.040; osmolality 800-900 mOsm/kg. (Book p741)

questions.q: The normal blood osmolality quoted beside the urine column is:
questions.exp: Blood osmolality 285-290 mOsm/kg against urine 800-900 mOsm/kg. (Book p741)

questions.q: In the acidification diagram, the cell and luminal pump responsible are:
opts: Alpha-intercalated cells of the cortical collecting duct with H+ ATPase
Principal cells of the cortical collecting duct with Na-K ATPase
Beta-intercalated cells of the proximal tubule with H+ ATPase
Podocytes of the glomerulus with aquaporin-2
questions.exp: Alpha-intercalated cells of cortical collecting duct (CCD) secrete H+ via the luminal H+ ATPase. (Book p741)

questions.q: Fill up: Secreted H+ buffered by NH3 forms the non-titratable, major acid ______.
questions.exp: NH3 + H+ → NH4+ : non titratable, major acid. (Book p741)

questions.q: Fill up: Buffering of secreted H+ by HPO4 2- yields the titratable acid ______.
questions.exp: HPO4 2- + H+ → H2PO4- : titratable acid. (Book p741)

questions.q: Urinary concentration rests on ADH from the posterior pituitary, the vasa recta and a medullary interstitium whose osmolality is raised by:
questions.exp: Medullary interstitium: ↑ osmolality d/t urea; ADH → free water reabsorption; vasa recta. (Book p741)

questions.q: A patient's urine pH stays above 5.5 for 3 days while the RFT remains normal. The label for this picture is:
questions.exp: Urine pH > 5.5 for 3 days + normal RFT → Type-1 renal tubular acidosis (RTA). (Book p741)

questions.q: Diabetes insipidus (dilute urine) is flagged when specific gravity and osmolality fall below:
questions.exp: Urine specific gravity < 1.005 and urine osmolality < 300 mOsm/kg → diabetes insipidus (↑ dilute urine). (Book p741)

questions.q: Isosthenuria, defined as urinary parameters equal to blood parameters, points to:
opts: Acute tubular necrosis and chronic tubulo-interstitial disease
Prerenal azotemia and bladder outlet obstruction
questions.exp: Isosthenuria (urinary parameters = blood parameters): ATN; chronic tubulo-interstitial disease (CTID). (Book p741)

questions.q: High colored urine may present as:
opts: Hematuria with red, pink, tea or cola colored urine
questions.exp: High colored urine can be hematuria, red, pink, tea, cola colored urine. (Book p742)

questions.q: The cause-wise split of high colored urine is urological, nephrological and hematological at:
questions.exp: Urological (90%), nephrological (9%), hematological (1%). (Book p742)

questions.q: The commonest urological cause highlighted for high colored urine is:
questions.exp: Urological (90%): carcinoma bladder (m/c). (Book p742)

questions.q: The hematological (1%) category of high colored urine corresponds to:
questions.exp: Hematological (1%): intravascular hemolysis. (Book p742)

questions.q: A red-tinged urine with a negative dipstick for blood should raise suspicion of:
questions.exp: Dipstick negative: porphyria; ↑ beetroot intake. (Book p742)

questions.q: The centrifugation step of the high-colored-urine approach uses:
questions.exp: Centrifugation of urine at 1600 rpm × 5 minutes. (Book p742)

questions.q: After centrifugation, a clear supernatant tells us that the colour came from:
questions.exp: Clear supernatant → RBC (settles down); high colored supernatant → pigments. (Book p742)

questions.q: All of the following define glomerular hematuria in the flowchart EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Glomerular hematuria: ≥ 40% dysmorphic RBCs / ≥ 5% acanthocytes / single RBC cast + proteinuria. (Book p742)

questions.q: Fill up: Glomerular hematuria criteria include ≥ 40 % dysmorphic RBCs or ≥ ______ % acanthocytes or a single RBC cast with proteinuria.
questions.exp: ≥ 40% dysmorphic RBCs / ≥ 5% acanthocytes / single RBC cast + proteinuria. (Book p742)

questions.q: Once glomerular hematuria is established, the next step in the flowchart is biopsy, which typically reveals:
questions.exp: Biopsy → mesangial disease (IgA nephropathy). (Book p742)

questions.q: The mechanism written for hematuria in IgA nephropathy is:
opts: Mesangial proliferation + matrix expansion → capillary rupture
questions.exp: Mesangial proliferation + matrix expansion → capillary rupture. (Book p742)

questions.q: When the settled RBCs point to a urological cause, the appropriate next step is:
opts: Radiological investigation with USG abdomen and CT
Cystoscopy with biopsy as first step
questions.exp: Urological cause → radiological Ix (USG abdomen, CT). (Book p742)

questions.q: A still high-colored supernatant is left undisturbed for how long before judging the colour?
questions.exp: Sample undisturbed for 3-6 hours, then observe whether the colour fades or persists. (Book p742)

questions.q: A crushed-limb injury patient passes dark urine; the supernatant colour fades over a few hours. The pigment and its source are:
questions.exp: Colour fades → myoglobin (short t½): rhabdomyolysis. (Book p742)

questions.q: Which statement about the standing-supernatant test is TRUE?
opts: A persistent colour implies hemoglobin with a long half-life from hemolysis
A persistent colour implies myoglobin from rhabdomyolysis
A fading colour implies hemoglobin from hemolysis
The test distinguishes porphyria from beetroot intake
questions.exp: Persistent colour → hemoglobin (long t½): hemolysis; fading → myoglobin (short t½). (Book p742)

questions.q: Match each urinary RBC description with its label — 1) Crenated, isomorphic cells 2) Dysmorphic cells 3) Acanthocytes … A) "Mickey mouse" RBCs B) Urological category C) Nephrological category
questions.exp: Urological: crenated, isomorphic; nephrological: dysmorphic; acanthocytes = Mickey mouse RBCs. (Book p743)

questions.q: The nephrological RBCs nicknamed after a famous cartoon mouse are:
questions.exp: Acanthocytes are called Mickey mouse RBCs, seen in the nephrological category. (Book p743)

questions.q: Which statement about the leukocyte/nitrite dipstick for UTI is TRUE?
opts: It has high specificity but poor sensitivity
It has high sensitivity but poor specificity
It is equally sensitive and specific
questions.exp: Leukocytes + nitrites for urinary tract infections: high specificity, poor sensitivity. (Book p743)

questions.q: A positive urobilinogen pad on the dipstick points to:
questions.exp: Urobilinogen on dipstick: extravascular hemolysis. (Book p743)

questions.q: A type-2 diabetic started on an SGLT2 inhibitor shows urine ketones; the glycemic pattern the book pairs with this drug is:
questions.exp: SGLT2 inhibitors: euglycemic ketosis (proximal RTA gives euglycemic glycosuria). (Book p743)

questions.q: Euglycemic glycosuria on the dipstick glucose row is the marker of:
questions.exp: Proximal RTA: euglycemic glycosuria. (Book p743)

questions.q: All of the following affect the leukocyte urine dipstick test EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Listed factors: concentrated urine, high relative density, proteinuria, glucosuria, cephalothin & tetracycline, cephalexin, tobramycin. (Book p743)

questions.q: Fill up: Cephalothin, tetracycline, cephalexin and tobramycin are listed as drugs affecting the urine ______ dipstick test.
questions.exp: These drugs are listed under factors affecting the leukocyte urine dipstick test. (Book p743)

questions.q: Which RBC-morphology statement is TRUE as per the figure?
opts: Crenated and isomorphic RBCs belong to the urological category
Crenated and isomorphic RBCs belong to the nephrological category
Dysmorphic RBCs belong to the urological category
questions.exp: Urological: crenated, isomorphic; nephrological: dysmorphic, acanthocytes. (Book p743)

questions.q: Uromodulin (Tamm-Horsfall protein) is produced by the:
opts: Thick ascending limb of loop of Henle
questions.exp: Produced by thick ascending limb of loop of Henle. (Book p744)

questions.q: The daily excretion of uromodulin quoted is:
questions.exp: Uromodulin/Tamm Horsfall protein: 70-80 mg/day. (Book p744)

questions.q: Which statement about uromodulin is TRUE?
opts: It is the most abundant component of normal urine and forms the matrix of casts
It is the most abundant component of normal plasma
It dissolves cast matrices in alkaline urine
It is excreted only in glomerular disease
questions.exp: Most abundant component of normal urine; forms matrix of casts. (Book p744)

questions.q: Match each urine protein range (mg/day) with its label — 1) <150 2) 150-500 3) >500 … A) Significant proteinuria B) Normal C) Functional proteinuria
questions.exp: <150 normal; 150-500 functional proteinuria; >500 significant proteinuria. (Book p744)

questions.q: An anxious student presents before exams with urine protein of 300 mg/day. The book's category for this level is:
questions.exp: 150-500 mg/day: functional proteinuria (stress, anxiety, menses, protein supplements). (Book p744)

questions.q: Fill up: In pregnancy, significant proteinuria is defined as urine protein greater than ______ mg/day.
questions.exp: >300 mg/day: significant proteinuria in pregnancy (vs >500 otherwise). (Book p744)

questions.q: The injury chain written for albuminuria runs: albumin → tubular injury → inflammation → ______ → fibrosis.
questions.exp: Albumin → tubular injury → inflammation → TGF-β → fibrosis. (Book p744)

questions.q: Microalbuminuria (moderately elevated albumin) spans urinary albumin of:
questions.exp: <30 normal; 30-300 microalbuminuria; >300 albuminuria. (Book p744)

questions.q: Moderately elevated urine albumin matters because it is a:
opts: Marker of vascular integrity with higher thrombosis (CVA, CAD) risk from endothelial injury
Marker of isolated lower urinary tract infection
Benign finding that needs no further evaluation
questions.exp: Marker of vascular integrity; ↑ risk of thrombosis (CVA, CAD) d/t endothelial injury; requires further evaluation. (Book p744)

questions.q: All of the following are listed tests for proteinuria EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Tests: 24 hour urine protein; spot PCR; spot ACR; urine dipstick test. (Book p744)

questions.q: The urine dipstick test turns positive only when proteinuria reaches roughly:
questions.exp: Dipstick: qualitative; positive only when there is ↑ proteinuria (~800 mg); detects only albumin. (Book p744)

questions.q: Fill up: Significant proteinuria in a non-pregnant adult is urine protein above ______ mg/day.
questions.exp: >500 mg/day: significant proteinuria. (Book p744)

questions.q: Which statement about the dipstick test for protein is TRUE?
opts: It detects only albumin and should be supplemented with PCR/ACR/24 hrs urine protein
It detects globulins better than albumin
It quantifies protein accurately in mg/day
It is positive at microalbuminuric levels
questions.exp: Dipstick detects only albumin; should be supplemented with PCR/ACR/24 hrs urine protein. (Book p744)

questions.q: The size order of urinary cells written is:
questions.exp: Cell size: RBC < WBC < epithelial cell. (Book p745)

questions.q: Tubular epithelial cells on microscopy are described with:
opts: Clear cytoplasm and round eccentric nucleus
questions.exp: Tubular epithelial cell with nucleus: granular cytoplasm & lobulated nucleus. (Book p745)

questions.q: Oval fat bodies under the polarizing microscope show the:
questions.exp: Polarizing microscope: Maltese cross appearance of oval fat bodies. (Book p745)

questions.q: The Maltese cross in the kidney is associated with all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.exp: In blood: babesiosis; in kidney: Fabry's, ADPKD, acute/chronic interstitial nephritis, prerenal azotemia. (Book p745)

questions.q: Phase contrast microscopy with monomorphic red cells in the figure illustrates the category of:
questions.exp: Phase contrast microscopy with monomorphic red cells corresponds to the urological pattern (vs dysmorphic/acanthocytes). (Book p745)

questions.q: On the phase-contrast photo, the arrow-labelled cell larger than the surrounding red cells is a:
questions.exp: The figure labels a large white cell among the monomorphic red cells (RBC < WBC < epithelial cell). (Book p745)

questions.q: Fill up: Urinary casts are formed in the ______.
questions.exp: Cast formation: distal convoluted tubule (DCT). (Book p745)

questions.q: Match each finding with its association — 1) Hyaline cast 2) Fine/coarse granular cast 3) Oval fat bodies … A) Maltese cross on polarizing microscopy B) Normal as well as kidney disease C) Kidney disease
questions.exp: Hyaline: normal + kidney disease; granular: kidney disease; oval fat bodies: Maltese cross. (Book p745)

questions.q: Hyaline casts are seen in:
questions.exp: Hyaline cast: normal; kidney disease. (Book p745)

questions.q: Coarse and fine granular casts signify:
questions.exp: Coarse/fine granular casts: kidney disease. (Book p745)

questions.q: Match each cast with its association — 1) RBC cast 2) WBC cast 3) Fatty cast … A) Lipiduria (nephrotic syndrome), Fabry's B) Glomerular hematuria C) Acute pyelonephritis, PSGN, ATN/AIN
questions.exp: RBC cast – glomerular hematuria; WBC cast – acute pyelonephritis, PSGN, ATN/AIN; fatty cast – lipiduria, Fabry's. (Book p746)

questions.q: Pigment fine granular casts point to pigment nephropathy caused by:
questions.exp: Pigment fine granular cast: pigment nephropathy – hemolysis; rhabdomyolysis. (Book p746)

questions.q: The cast described as most specific for ATN/AIN is the:
questions.exp: Tubular epithelial cast (muddy brown): ATN/AIN (most specific). (Book p746)

questions.q: Broad casts and waxy casts are the markers of:
questions.exp: Broad cast and waxy cast: chronic kidney disease. (Book p746)

questions.q: Fractured casts, seen on biopsy, are associated with:
questions.exp: Fractured cast (on biopsy): myeloma. (Book p746)

questions.q: A patient with drug-induced interstitial injury shows casts packed with eosinophils. The association listed is:
questions.exp: Eosinophil cast: ATN/AIN. (Book p746)

questions.q: Pigment nephropathy with pigment fine granular casts arises from all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Pigment nephropathy: hemolysis, rhabdomyolysis; nephrotic syndrome instead gives fatty casts/lipiduria. (Book p746)

questions.q: Fill up: The muddy brown cast of ATN/AIN is a ______ cast.
questions.exp: Tubular epithelial cast (muddy brown): ATN/AIN (most specific). (Book p746)

questions.q: Which cast statement is TRUE as per the table?
opts: WBC casts occur in acute pyelonephritis, post-streptococcal GN and ATN/AIN
WBC casts are specific for chronic kidney disease
questions.exp: WBC cast: acute pyelonephritis; PSGN; ATN/AIN. RBC cast = glomerular hematuria; waxy = CKD. (Book p746)

questions.q: Match each cast with its association — 1) Broad & waxy casts 2) Fractured cast (on biopsy) 3) Eosinophil cast … A) ATN/AIN B) Myeloma C) Chronic kidney disease
questions.exp: Broad/waxy – CKD; fractured – myeloma; eosinophil – ATN/AIN. (Book p746)

questions.q: Fatty casts are associated with:
questions.exp: Fatty cast: lipiduria (nephrotic syndrome); Fabry's. (Book p746)

questions.q: Match each crystal with its shape — 1) Uric acid 2) Calcium oxalate dihydrate 3) Struvite (MgNH4PO4) … A) Coffin lid appearance B) Rhomboid crystals C) Bipyramidal / envelope shaped
questions.exp: Uric acid – rhomboid; calcium oxalate dihydrate – bipyramidal/envelope; struvite – coffin lid. (Book p747)

questions.q: Match each crystal with its description — 1) Calcium oxalate monohydrate 2) Calcium phosphate 3) Cystine … A) Hexagonal crystal B) Dumb bell shaped C) Star shaped in alkaline urine
questions.exp: Calcium oxalate monohydrate – dumb bell; calcium phosphate – star shaped (alkaline urine); cystine – hexagonal. (Book p747)

questions.q: The coffin-lid crystal with the formula MgNH4PO4 is:
questions.exp: Struvite (MgNH4PO4): coffin lid appearance. (Book p747)

questions.q: Star-shaped crystals forming in alkaline urine are:
questions.exp: Calcium phosphate (in alkaline urine): star shaped. (Book p747)

questions.q: All of the following crystal-shape pairs are as printed EXCEPT:
opts: Calcium oxalate monohydrate - dumb bell shaped
questions.exp: Uric acid crystals are rhomboid; envelope shape belongs to calcium oxalate dihydrate. (Book p747)

questions.q: The broom brush appearance on urine microscopy belongs to crystals of:
questions.exp: Amoxicillin crystal: broom brush appearance. (Book p747)

questions.q: Fill up: The hexagonal crystals seen on urine microscopy are ______ crystals.
questions.exp: Hexagonal cystine crystal. (Book p747)

questions.q: Which crystal statement is TRUE as per the figure labels?
opts: Calcium oxalate monohydrate is dumb bell shaped while the dihydrate is envelope shaped
Calcium oxalate monohydrate is envelope shaped while the dihydrate is dumb bell shaped
questions.exp: Monohydrate – dumb bell; dihydrate – bipyramidal/envelope; cholesterol crystals are listed without those shapes. (Book p747)

questions.q: A stone former's microscopy shows bipyramidal, envelope-shaped crystals. The crystal type is:
questions.exp: Calcium oxalate dihydrate: bipyramidal/envelope shaped. (Book p747)

units.title: Urine collection & sample handling
units.guide: First-morning midstream sample, 2-4 h analysis window with immediate pH, formaldehyde/glutaraldehyde preservation, 2-8°C × 12 h storage, and the avoid-list (72 h strenuous exercise, menstruation, urobag sampling).

units.title: Physical properties: colour & appearance
units.guide: The colour table line by line: light yellow normal, pale/white with water loading, pink (desferrioxamine, beetroot), darkening on standing (imipenem + cilastatin), green (triamterene), brown (nitrofurantoin), orange (rifampicin, entacapone).

units.title: Physical properties: odour table
units.guide: Every odour-disease pair: pungent (infection/ammonia), musty (PKU), curry/maple syrup (MSUD), sweaty feet (isovaleric acidemia, glutaric aciduria II), cabbage/rancid butter (tyrosinemia 1), cat urine (MCD), acid (MMA), fish (trimethylaminuria), sulfurous (cystinuria), sweet (beta ketothiolase deficiency), swimming pool (hawkinsinuria).

units.title: Other properties & tubular regulation
units.guide: Urine vs blood pH/SG/osmolality, CCD alpha-intercalated H+ ATPase acidification with NH4+ (non-titratable) and H2PO4- (titratable) acids, ADH-urea-vasa recta concentration, and the abnormal-value table (type-1 RTA, DI, isosthenuria).

units.title: High colored urine: causes & dipstick gate
units.guide: Red/pink/tea/cola urine with the 90/9/1 cause split (carcinoma bladder m/c; intravascular hemolysis), dipstick-negative mimics (porphyria, beetroot) and the 1600 rpm × 5 min centrifugation step.

units.title: Supernatant flowchart: RBC vs pigment
units.guide: Clear supernatant → RBCs; glomerular hematuria criteria (≥40% dysmorphic, ≥5% acanthocytes, single RBC cast + proteinuria) → biopsy → IgA nephropathy mechanism; urological arm → USG/CT; standing test separating myoglobin (fades) from hemoglobin (persists).

units.title: RBC morphology & dipstick parameters
units.guide: Urological crenated/isomorphic vs nephrological dysmorphic/acanthocytes (Mickey mouse RBCs), leukocyte + nitrite specificity, urobilinogen → extravascular hemolysis, glucose-row euglycemic glycosuria/ketosis, and the leukocyte-dipstick interference list.

units.title: Proteinuria: uromodulin & protein levels
units.guide: Tamm-Horsfall protein (70-80 mg/day, TAL origin, cast matrix) and the protein thresholds: <150 normal, 150-500 functional, >500 significant, >300 significant in pregnancy.

units.title: Albuminuria & tests for proteinuria
units.guide: Albumin → TGF-β → fibrosis chain, microalbuminuria 30-300 vs albuminuria >300, vascular-integrity significance, and the four tests with dipstick limits (~800 mg threshold, albumin-only detection).

units.title: Microscopic examination & oval fat bodies
units.guide: Cell size ladder (RBC < WBC < epithelial), tubular epithelial cell features, phase-contrast monomorphic picture, and oval fat bodies with the Maltese cross list (babesiosis in blood; Fabry's, ADPKD, interstitial nephritis, prerenal azotemia in kidney).

units.title: Casts: formation & basic types
units.sec: Casts in Urine - Formation & Basics · p745
units.guide: Cast formation in the DCT, hyaline (normal + disease) vs granular (kidney disease) casts, woven into the microscopy unit's page order.

units.title: Casts: specific clinical associations
units.sec: Casts in Urine - Specific Associations · p746
units.guide: The full cast table: pigment fine granular (hemolysis/rhabdo), RBC (glomerular hematuria), WBC (pyelonephritis/PSGN/ATN-AIN), muddy brown tubular epithelial (most specific ATN/AIN), broad & waxy (CKD), fatty (lipiduria/Fabry's), eosinophil (ATN/AIN) and fractured (myeloma).

units.title: Crystals in urine
units.guide: Every crystal-shape label: uric acid rhomboid, Ca-oxalate dihydrate envelope/bipyramidal, monohydrate dumb bell, Ca-phosphate star (alkaline), struvite coffin lid, cholesterol, amoxicillin broom brush and hexagonal cystine.
